title: Evidence-based answer
summary: Require support for each substantive claim rather than a list of impressive links.

sections.label: Claim record
items: Atomic claim and its status: observed, inferred, proposed, or unresolved.
Exact source identifier, passage/section, and version.
Scope that affects the claim. This might be a software version and environment, or a jurisdiction, population and effective period for a domain assertion.

sections.label: Verification layers
sections.text: A working link proves availability, not support. A relevant passage may still fail to support the claim. A supported claim may still be inapplicable to the requested scope.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: The reader can reproduce the evidential basis. Missing support leads to a useful uncertainty statement rather than a fabricated answer.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Requirements and evidence, Tests and review, Recommend go or no-go. Use when drafting evidence requirements, reviewing claim support and writing a recommendation that exposes remaining uncertainty. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Produce a claim table with a status, exact passage, source version and relevant scope for each substantive conclusion.
Check output to obtain: Sample a supported, contradicted and unsupported claim. Record the source-to-claim comparison rather than only link availability.
Check output to obtain: Keep unanswered claims and their decision owner visible in the recommendation.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: Reviewed on 2026-10-15: PROV-O defines derivation, primary-source and quotation relationships. This vocabulary supports traceable evidence links. The answer contract, claim statuses and acceptance policy remain Atlas recommendations, not requirements imposed by PROV-O. Only this added factual contribution was checked in this review. Earlier sections retain their stated proposed or illustrative basis.

catalog.applicability: Use this when an answer or finding must carry support for each substantive claim, with its status, exact source, scope and uncertainty. A working link, a relevant passage and a supported claim are different layers, and missing support should produce an uncertainty statement rather than a fabricated answer.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.

claims.text: PROV-O defines derivation, primary-source and quotation relationships.
